title: Coronary artery (atherosclerosis)
description: A coronary artery cut across, with atherosclerosis: the intima is thickened all the way round, and much more on one side, where a plaque with inflammatory cells and foam cells has formed. The lumen is still wide.
look_for: The lumen, which is still wide in this vessel
The plaque: a thickened intima on one side of the wall, with inflammatory cells and foam cells near the lumen
Compare the thinner wall on the opposite side (its intima is a little thickened too)
Tunica media (smooth muscle) beneath the intima, and the adventitia outside it
